articles.title: Community Day reaches 97 meetups across more than 30 countries
articles.dek: Two days before the November 7 gathering, the event directory helps attendees find a local meetup and sign up.
body: Open Home Foundation Community Day is this Saturday, November 7. In the Home Assistant release notes, Franck Nijhof puts the worldwide programme at 97 meetups across more than 30 countries. He plans to join the gathering in Enschede.
The foundation’s event map helps people find a gathering nearby. Each listing in the Community Day registration directory links to the local event, where attendees can check the details and sign up.

articles.title: ESPHome devices can carry a recovery copy of their configuration
articles.dek: Makers can opt to embed their project files in the firmware and retrieve them through an encrypted connection.
body: An ESPHome device can hold a recovery copy of the configuration used to build it. Makers enable the option before flashing. The firmware stores the main YAML configuration together with included files and packages. A compatible client can then request the compressed files from the running device.

By default, retrieval requires an encrypted connection. The saved configuration keeps the file structure and replaces recognized passwords and keys with placeholders the owner can fill in. Credentials assembled in other ways can still appear in the copy. Makers who explicitly include secrets get the files exactly as written.

pullRequests.title: [store_yaml] Embed user YAML in firmware for recovery

articles.title: Mark a passage in a book or podcast and return to it
articles.dek: Music Assistant’s web player saves named bookmarks alongside chapters and lets each listener keep their own.
body: A listener can mark a moment in an audiobook or podcast episode in Music Assistant’s fullscreen player, then return to it from the book or episode page. A bookmark can have a name, and its marker on the timeline shows its position and chapter.

Bookmarks belong to the listener and to a particular copy of the book or episode. Audiobookshelf keeps its audiobook bookmarks in sync with its own apps. Music Assistant stores bookmarks locally for library copies when the provider does not support them, including Audiobookshelf podcast episodes. The web controls require server interface version 102.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps Marketplace downloads working in mainland China
articles.dek: HACS China users carry their community mirrors into the upgrade, and other installations can choose them in Settings.
body: The Marketplace can download its catalogue and community projects through mirrors run by the Home Assistant China community. Home Assistant recognizes existing HACS China installations during migration and keeps them on the mirrors, so their downloads can continue without a VPN.

The Marketplace menu also lets owners choose GitHub or the China mirrors. A fresh installation configured for China offers the choice if it cannot reach the catalogue. HACS China’s shared-pool credentials are discarded during migration. Owners keep their personal GitHub tokens, and the Marketplace keeps those tokens out of requests to the mirror.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s AI can schedule commands from any client
articles.dek: A delayed request runs with the permissions of the person who gave it.
body: Home Assistant gives AI conversation agents a way to schedule a request such as turning the lights off in five minutes. Previously, delayed commands were offered only on devices that supported timers. The agent supplies a self-contained instruction because Home Assistant starts a fresh conversation when the time comes.

Home Assistant also carries the requester’s identity into the delayed action. Previously it ran without a user, which skipped entity permission checks and left the logbook without the name of the person who asked. The scheduled action now respects that person’s access and links back to the original request.

articles.title: Home Assistant restarts faster when a camera stream stalls
articles.dek: On a tested Bambu Lab printer camera, a restart with the stream open fell from 241 seconds to 33.
body: Home Assistant can stop a camera stream even when the camera keeps sending video frames with frozen timestamps. Previously the stream waited for a usable frame before checking whether it should stop. An idle camera connection could stay open indefinitely, and a Home Assistant restart could wait through several shutdown timeouts.

The contributor measured a restart on Home Assistant OS with a Bambu Lab P2S camera open at 33 seconds after the correction, down from 241 seconds. A separate local camera stream reproduced the same failure when its timestamps stopped advancing.

pullRequests.title: Stop stream worker while discarding invalid packets

articles.title: Z-Wave JS queues updates for several sleeping devices
articles.dek: An update waiting for one battery-powered device to wake up no longer blocks requests for the others.
body: Z-Wave JS 15.32.1 lets applications request firmware updates from the update service for several devices in one pass. Previously, asking to update a sleeping device reserved the network-wide slot until that device woke up and finished. The next request could fail even when it targeted a different device.

The driver also reports whether the device being checked has an update in progress. It still refuses a second update for the same device and protects the controller while its own firmware is being updated.

fix: only report an OTA firmware update in progress for the node being updated

articles.title: Move a block of playlist tracks together in Music Assistant
articles.dek: Supported playlists gain drag handles, keyboard moves and shortcuts to send a selection to either end.
body: Music Assistant’s web interface lets playlist editors move one track or a selection of tracks while preserving the order within the selection. Drag handles appear in the playlist’s own order when search and filters are clear. The up and down arrows move a focused track one place at a time.

Move to top and Move to bottom also work from a sorted view. Editing requires a writable playlist whose connected sources support reordering. Tidal supports moving a selection in one request. If the save fails, the list returns to the order held by the music provider.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps repair notices with the right connection
articles.dek: Separate accounts, addresses and servers keep their own warnings when another setup is removed.
body: Home Assistant separates repair notices that used to overwrite one another when several connections had the same problem. Removing one setup could also clear a warning that still mattered for another. The affected notices now follow the connection they describe.

For example, two Rova waste-collection addresses in the same postcode get separate warnings with the full address. Removing a Fressnapf account also preserves the warning on another account that shares its tracker. Disabling a connection hides the notices linked to it.

articles.title: Battery-free Friends of Hue switches gain button events in ZHA
articles.dek: The EnOcean module used by several switch makers reports both presses and releases.
body: ZHA’s device handlers recognize the EnOcean PTM 215Z module found in Friends of Hue wall switches from makers including Senic and Gira, NodOn, Vimar and Niko. These switches could previously pair as an unidentified device with no button entities for automations.

Each of the four rocker contacts reports when it is pressed and released. Pressing the two upper contacts together, or the two lower ones, sends events for both. The handler was checked with a Senic/Gira Friends of Hue switch.

articles.title: Wyoming voice agents can listen for a reply without another wake word
articles.dek: An agent signals that it expects a reply, allowing compatible Assist satellites to listen again.
body: A conversation agent connected through Wyoming can tell Home Assistant when a spoken response calls for an answer. On a compatible Assist satellite such as Voice Preview Edition, the listener can answer the question without repeating the wake word.

The decision comes from the agent that asked the question. Home Assistant passes its request to continue through to the satellite. Existing agents that send no such signal still finish the turn normally. Andrea Genovese makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with this work.

articles.title: SMLIGHT devices start locally while Home Assistant checks for updates
articles.dek: A slow or unreachable online firmware catalogue no longer holds up reachable devices after a restart.
body: Home Assistant brings an SMLIGHT device’s local controls and readings online before looking up available firmware. Previously the integration waited for the online catalogue first, even when the device was already reachable on the home network.

The firmware check runs in the background. Update entities retain information such as the installed version when a catalogue request fails. The integration can pick up the available firmware on its next daily check or a manual refresh.

articles.title: ESPHome extends browser access checks to device updates
articles.dek: A read-only dashboard on another website may need permission to receive live updates from an ESP32.
body: ESPHome applies its list of permitted websites to more of a device’s web interface, including firmware uploads, Prometheus metrics and the live event stream on ESP32. A browser page hosted elsewhere must be on that list to make those requests.

A read-only dashboard that uses the ESP32 event stream may need its site added to the existing allowed-origins setting. Dashboards that already have permission to control entities use the same list. Server-side scrapers and scripts that send no browser origin continue to work.

pullRequests.title: [web_server_base] Apply the web server's allowed origins check to every handler

articles.title: ZHA corrects the service-life warning on NOUS gas detectors
articles.dek: A healthy E9 could show a problem with its sensor lifetime as soon as it was paired.
body: ZHA corrects the replacement warning reported by the NOUS E9 gas detector. The E9 reports one value while its sensor is within its service life and the opposite value at the end. ZHA interpreted them backwards, marking a healthy unit as having a problem.

The existing diagnostic entity keeps its identity and now reports a problem when the detector indicates the end of its service life. This correction concerns the replacement indicator, separate from gas detection itself.

pullRequests.title: Fix inverted lifecycle sensor for NOUS E9 gas detector

articles.title: Choose when a Music Assistant player stops for the night
articles.dek: An optional clock control shows when playback is due to stop and lets an automation choose the time.
body: Home Assistant adds a sleep-timer clock to each Music Assistant player. After enabling the control, an owner can read the timer’s local end time or choose a new one from a dashboard or automation. Changes made in Music Assistant update the same control.
Choose a time that has already passed today and the timer runs until that time tomorrow. The entity starts disabled, so owners can enable it for the players where they want it.

pullRequests.title: Add Music Assistant sleep timer time entity
